test_title: SSC Stenographer 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 13 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
The following sentence has been divided into segments. One of them may contain an error. Select the segment that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

Two people were / fighting to each other / for no reason.
solution:
The correct answer is '**fighting to each other'**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the use of the preposition **"to"** instead of the correct preposition **"with"** before **"each other"**.
 
• In English, the correct phrase is **"fighting with each other"** to indicate a mutual conflict.
 
• Using **"to"** in this context is grammatically incorrect and changes the intended meaning.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **Option 1** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Two people were **fighting with each other** for no reason."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Two people were** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **fighting with each other** – This is the corrected part of the sentence.
 
• **for no reason.** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **No error** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in Option 1.
